caption: Khal Anshei Tallymawr Inc. v. Township of Toms River
citation_line: Khal Anshei Tallymawr Inc. v. Township of Toms River, Nos. 3:21-cv-02716 & 3:21-cv-03239, ECF No. 168 (D.N.J. Aug. 8, 2024)
headnote_district_ruling: Entered a protective order blocking discovery sought through nineteen nonparty subpoenas in consolidated religious-land-use cases. The requests were irrelevant, insufficiently tied to alleged anti-Semitic animus, and unduly burdensome, though the subpoenas were not formally quashed.
qualification_rationale: A developed proportionality analysis for sprawling third-party discovery in RLUIPA and constitutional zoning litigation.
appellate_posture_note: Non-dispositive discovery order; no substantive appellate review identified.
subject_screen_exclusion_reason: Protective order concerning nonparty subpoenas; the RLUIPA and constitutional merits remain undecided.
